overview: A Pacific system brings snow to the northern Rockies Friday into Saturday, with the Pacific Northwest and Cascades wet through Friday. A calmer break follows over the weekend. Another round of storms reaches the West Coast and the Sierra early next week.

regions.title: Northern Rockies
regions.text: A Pacific system moves into western Wyoming Thursday night and Friday, bringing light to moderate snow west of the Continental Divide. A second wave Friday night into Saturday brings wider snow and strong westerly wind, with the first light snow of the season possible east of the Divide. Grand Targhee leads with 67 inches in total and its biggest day is Saturday, with 27 inches.

regions.title: Cascades
regions.text: A weak to moderate atmospheric river brings steady rain and snow Thursday and Friday, with snow levels dropping Friday night into Saturday. Mt. Bachelor leads with 46 inches in total and its biggest day is Thursday, with 19 inches. Winds of 30 to 35 mph are likely Thursday morning in the Blue Mountains, so high-profile vehicles should take care.

regions.title: Coast Mountains
regions.text: Rain and showers dominate Thursday and Friday before a drier stretch. Whistler is the top resort with 33 inches in total, its biggest day Thursday with 16 inches. Showers and flurries return Sunday and Monday.

regions.title: Northeast
regions.text: A winter weather advisory covers Thursday evening through Friday morning for freezing rain across northern New York and central Vermont, so roads may be slick. Jay Peak leads with 27 inches in total and its biggest day is Friday, with 12 inches. Another frontal system brings rain and snow Sunday night into Monday.

regions.title: Kootenays
regions.text: Rain changes to snow at higher elevations on Thanksgiving, with a snow level near 1,500 meters. Whitewater leads with 23 inches in total and its biggest day is Thursday, with 16 inches. Showers and flurries continue through the weekend and into Monday.

regions.title: Central Rockies
regions.text: Dry, mild weather holds through Thanksgiving. A northwest flow brings snow to the Park Range Friday evening through Saturday night, and the storm could reach down toward Vail Pass. Steamboat leads with 26 inches in total and its biggest day is Saturday, with 20 inches.

regions.title: Wasatch
regions.text: A weak system brushes northern Utah Friday night into Saturday, bringing light snow mainly north of I-80. Powder Mountain leads with 16 inches in total and its biggest day is Saturday, with 8 inches. More light snow is expected Sunday night into Monday.

regions.title: Tahoe
regions.text: Dry, seasonable weather continues through the weekend, with dense valley fog likely. Rain and snow return Sunday and Monday, with snow above about 7,000 feet. Sugar Bowl leads with 14 inches in total and its biggest day is Sunday, with 10 inches. The Weather Prediction Center says the storms could be heavy along the California coast on Tuesday.

regions.title: Okanagan
regions.text: Showers end early Thursday, with a mix of sun and cloud Friday and Saturday. Showers and flurries return Sunday and continue into Monday. Big White leads with 14 inches in total and its biggest day is Thursday, with 10 inches.

regions.title: Canadian Rockies
regions.text: Showers on Thursday turn to a mix of sun and cloud and light flurries later in the week, with temperatures dropping. Sunshine Village leads with 8 inches in total, all on Thursday.

ahead.text: The Weather Prediction Center expects heavy rain and snow along the California coast on Tuesday Dec 1.

sources.name: NOAA buoys 51001 / 51101 (method: Powder Buoy, Mike Ruzek)

buoy.text: Buoys 51001 and 51101 near Hawaii popped Nov 25, the swell signal Powder Buoy watches for a Wasatch storm about two weeks later — here Dec 6–12. In past winters a pop raised the chance of a Wasatch storm in that window by roughly 6 to 12 points. Experimental: promising, not proven.
